explanation: The left hand is traditionally considered unclean in Thailand, so food eaten directly by hand (like sticky rice) and anything passed or received, such as money, should use the right hand. This mainly matters when eating without utensils; at an ordinary meal Thais conventionally hold the fork in the left hand and the spoon in the right, so using your left hand to push food onto the spoon is completely normal.
local_tip: Use your right hand for anything eaten by hand or passed to someone, but don't worry about which hand holds your fork — spoon in the right, fork in the left, is standard Thai table manners.

also_check.note: Eating with the left hand is considered highly impolite, as it is reserved for personal hygiene.
The left hand is reserved for hygiene and should not be used for eating or passing food.
Hand-eating is rare and chopstick use makes which hand you favor largely irrelevant.
